newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money and deposits seen in uptrend.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money and deposits seen in uptrend.

text.p: Dutch call money rates remained high, and dealers expected them to cling to their current levels amid liquidty jitters.
Deposits also started to rise as a result of the dollar's strength against European currencies and amid fears Germany would hike rates to support the mark, dealers said.
"There is a fear in the market of a rate rise (in Germany), but to me, it seems only a panic reaction," said one dealer.
Deposits rose four to eight basis points with three-month paper bid at 3.20 percent.
Call money was bid between 3.25 to 3.50 percent, with occasional settlements at even higher levels.
Dealers also noted commercial banks were probably not used to the new money market instruments introduced by the central bank in May.
"Players are very cautious and to me, it seems that especially smaller banks struggle a little with the new policy," said one dealer.
Another dealer said call money had been bid at the usual level of just under 3.00 percent when the first month-long cash reserve period started last May.
"This call money remains at a dramatically high level," he said.
The guilder was stable versus the German mark at 112.585 per 100 marks from 112.580 on Monday.
It was weaker against the dollar, trading around 2.025 guilders versus almost 2.017 yesterday.
